title: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)
summary: FTP is a client-server protocol for file transfer. Control connection (port 21, text commands): USER, PASS, CWD, PWD, LIST, RETR, STOR, DELE, MKD, RMD, QUIT, PASV, PORT, TYPE, MODE, STRU. Data connection (port 20 or passive port): transfers file data. Two modes: active (server connects to client) and passive (client connects to server).

structure.meaning: Text-based command/response. Commands: USER, PASS, CWD, PWD, LIST, RETR, STOR, DELE, MKD, RMD, QUIT, PASV, PORT, TYPE (A/I), MODE (S/B/C), STRU (F/R/P).
Transfers file data. Active: server connects to client's port. Passive: client connects to server's port (PASV response gives IP+port).
1xx preliminary, 2xx success, 3xx intermediate, 4xx transient error, 5xx permanent error. E.g., 220 (service ready), 230 (logged in), 226 (transfer complete), 530 (not logged in).
TYPE A (ASCII, converts line endings), TYPE I (Image/binary, no conversion).
Client sends PASV; server responds with IP and port (h1,h2,h3,h4,p1,p2). Client connects to that address.

notes: FTP uses two TCP connections: control (port 21) and data (port 20 or passive).
Active mode: server connects to client (problematic with NAT/firewalls).
Passive mode: client connects to server (firewall-friendly).
FTPS (FTP over TLS) adds encryption. SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) is a different protocol over SSH.
FTP is largely superseded by SFTP/SCP for security.
